title: Control-plane rollback safeguards and tenanted load-shedding policy
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Objective: Reduce blast radius and customer-visible disruption during control-plane upgrades, node failures, and cross-region incidents for Dedicated/Private deployments. Deliverables: (1) per-tenant admission & circuit-breaker policies bound to isolated control-plane partitions, (2) staged rollback/rollback-safeguards for control-plane deployments that avoid mass tenant eviction, (3) a tenanted load-shedding policy that ties to SLO tiers and dynamic tenant scoring, (4) multi-region failover playbook with safe-prefetching and KV-cache rehydration procedures.

Background: Recent outage post upgrade showed concurrent control-plane rollouts plus a noisy tenant caused cascading restarts in several Dedicated clusters. Current rolling-upgrade logic is region-wide and lacks tenant-scoped throttles; circuit breakers are global which forces large failovers. This ticket scopes engineering work to provide safer, tenant-aware controls and automated rollback behavior that preserves SLOs for high-tier customers while allowing controlled degradation for lower tiers.

Design summary:
- Admission & Circuit Breaker: implement a tenant-scoped admission controller that tracks on-the-wire concurrency, queued requests, p95/p99 latency per-tenant, and error rate. Circuit-breaker thresholds are parameterized by customer SLO tier (gold/silver/bronze). When thresholds are crossed, the controller applies graduated actions: local request shedding, soft 429s with Retry-After, KV-cache bypass for cached prefixes, and finally hard rejects.
- Staged rollback-safeguards: introduce a two-stage rollback workflow for control-plane deploys. Stage 1: automatic per-pool rollback for unhealthy pods with a cooldown and tenant affinity preservation. Stage 2: cascade rollback to pool/region only if health does not recover within the cooldown window. Maintain per-tenant session pins for up to N minutes during rollback to avoid session stomping.
- Tenant scoring & load-shedding policy: compute a real-time tenant score (importance, current error budget remaining, spike factor, recent rollout exposure). The load-shedding policy uses this score plus quota & classes to make shedding decisions; high-score tenants are routed to canary lanes or preserved KV-cache priming.
- Multi-region failover & cache rehydration: safe failover requires preserving KV cache hot-sets. When we shift tenants between regions, we prefetch most-used prefixes to minimize latency/quality regression. A fast metadata sync provides tenant routing hints while the full state is being rehydrated asynchronously.

Metrics & SLOs:
- Per-tenant error_rate_5m, p99_latency_1m, admit_rejects_1m, shed_count_1h, rollback_rate_24h.
- SLO mapping: Gold: p99 < 200ms, error_rate < 0.1%; Silver: p99 < 400ms, error_rate < 0.5%; Bronze: p99 < 750ms, error_rate < 1.5%.
- Alerting: when >5% of gold tenants exceed their error budget in 30 minutes OR when aggregate shed_count crosses threshold, trigger oncall + automatic canary rollback.

Runbook (summary):
1) Detection: observability detects sustained p99 regressions or cascading restarts.
2) Isolation: admission controller enters partial-shed mode targeting noisy tenants.
3) Containment: freeze new control-plane rollouts in affected region; evaluate per-pool health.
4) Recovery: attempt per-pool rollback; if failure persists, runstage-2 rollback and use traffic reroute to warm standby region.
5) Postmortem: gather decision artifacts, list tenants impacted, propose follow-ups.

Tradeoffs discussed:
- Complexity vs. predictability: per-tenant logic adds state and more code paths in the control plane. We mitigate by scoping state to short-lived scoring and keeping core routing deterministic.
- Consistency vs. latency: preserving session pins during rollbacks may increase temporary latency on some requests. We prioritize tenant SLO tiers to balance.
- Cost: prefetching and maintaining warmed caches in standby regions increases cross-region egress and storage. We'll gate warm-sets by tenant score and configurable budget.

Implementation plan (high level):
A) Spike (2w): prototype tenant score and local admission policy; simulate noisy-tenant behavior in staging.
B) Circuit breaker & shedding (3w): wire into request path with feature flag; include observability; add metrics.
C) Rollback-safeguards (3w): implement two-stage rollback, session pin tracking, and staged drain.
D) Multi-region rehydration (4w): implement warm-set prefetch and safe routing with fallback.
E) Chaos & verification (2w): run graduated chaos (pod restarts, region partition) in staging, run cost analysis.

Testing & verification: create workload harness for synthetic tenants (noisy, bursty, gold/silver/bronze) and validate: percent of gold tenants kept within SLO during induced failure, rollback_rate and shed_count vs baseline. Define acceptance criteria and create automated regression tests.

Follow-ups & open questions:
- How long can we reasonably pin sessions without violating consistency requirements for private deployments? (action: research by SDK/Client team)
- Should warm-set prefetching be limited by tenant budget rather than global budget? (PM decision pending)
- Integration with Dedicated autoscaler: should admission shedding feed back to autoscaler to request burst capacity?

Acceptance criteria:
- Staging runs show gold tenants maintain >=99% of baseline SLO under simulated noisy-tenant events.
- Circuit breaker metrics and alerts available in production telemetry.
- Code landed behind feature flag and exercised by two oncall drills.

Estimated effort: 12 engineering sprints (split across runtime, control-plane, and infra).
